sets.title: Everyday Science
sets.description: Three quick questions about the physical world.

questions.passage: At sea level, water boils at 100 °C (212 °F).
questions.question: At what temperature does water boil at sea level?
questions.explanation: At standard atmospheric pressure, water boils at 100 °C, which is the same temperature as 212 °F.
explanations: 0 °C is the freezing point of water, not its boiling point.
50 °C is well below boiling at sea level.
Correct. At sea level, water boils at 100 °C.
212 °C is much hotter than boiling water; 212 °F is the Fahrenheit equivalent of 100 °C.

questions.question: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere; oxygen is about 21%.
explanations: Correct. Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere.
Oxygen is the second most abundant gas, at about 21%.
Carbon dioxide is present in only trace amounts.
Argon is a noble gas present in small amounts.

questions.question: Which force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the attractive force between masses; the Sun's gravity keeps the planets in orbit.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was chosen as Australia's capital in 1908 as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
explanations: Sydney is Australia's largest city, but it is not the capital.
Correct. Canberra is the capital of Australia.
Melbourne is a large city, but it is not the capital.
Perth is the capital of Western Australia, not of the country.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean covers more area than all of Earth's land combined.

questions.question: On which continent is the Sahara Desert located?
questions.explanation: The Sahara spans much of northern Africa and is the largest hot desert in the world.
